title: RD hover: S Pen hover sticks to far-left x=0 on Display 2 (multi-monitor boundary)
description: After the 120fps/native-cursor change, S Pen hover only moves the host cursor correctly on the primary display. On Display 2 the cursor gets stuck at the far-left edge of the primary screen. Suspected coordinate-mapping/_desktopLeft offset bug in the Stage-3 pointer bridge (EnqueuePointerSampleAsInputEvent) and/or Android hover coordinate computation.
close_reason: Root cause: double application of the host desktop offset. Android mapLocalToHost already returns absolute virtual-desktop coords (relativeX*hostW + hostLeft, RemoteDesktopScreen.kt:521), and the host DispatchInput re-added _desktopLeft/_desktopTop (RemoteDesktopHandler.cs:750/757/765), so on a non-zero-origin secondary monitor the cursor was driven off-screen and SendInput clamped it to the desktop edge (x=0). Fix: removed the host-side offset addition (Android coords are already absolute); deleted the now-dead _desktopLeft/_desktopTop fields. Primary monitor unaffected (origin 0,0). Host builds clean.

title: Remote commands fail at cold boot — Session-0 agent + GUI-host port-takeover reliability
description:
Symptom: after a cold boot the Android client connects but remote commands don't execute (worse at the login screen; flaky after login).

Architecture (confirmed): RemEx.Host runs in two roles — (1) headless --agent as the LocalSystem Windows Service 'RemexHost' in Session 0 (command plane + telemetry, NO desktop streaming), and (2) an interactive GUI host launched at user login that TAKES OVER the canonical port from the agent via the RemExHostControl named pipe (HostControlServer/HostControlClient/AgentCoordinator), then serves the full host in the user session.

Root contributors found this session:
1. Triple-launch collision: service (artifacts/publish, SYSTEM) + HKCU Run GUI host (C:\Program Files, Connor) + a manual dev run (artifacts/bin) all ran at once -> port fallback 5005->5007 / 8338->8340 and RemexIPC/RemExLocalIPC 'Access denied' retry spam. Killed the two extras live.
2. Build split-brain: the Service binary (artifacts/publish, 06/15 14:43) and the login GUI host binary (C:\Program Files, 06/15 00:21, ~14h older) are different builds. The Program Files copy predates today's machine-wide-storage + SCM-double-registration fixes.
3. Session 0 isolation: the agent alone cannot run Lock / MonitorOff / SignOut / desktop streaming (no interactive desktop). LaunchApp uses WTSQueryUserToken+CreateProcessAsUser (works only once a user is logged in). Power commands (shutdown/restart/sleep/hibernate) work from the agent regardless.

Disproved: pipe ACLs are NOT the blocker — interactive user Connor can connect to RemExHostControl/RemExLocalIPC/RemexIPC created by the SYSTEM service (verified by direct NamedPipeClientStream.Connect).

Next: clean cold-boot capture (process list + listening ports + /debug/logs) with only the service + single login GUI host, after unifying to one current build/location, to confirm the takeover path completes.
notes: MAJOR PROGRESS 2026-06-16: Root duplicate/split-brain fixed (RemEx-nx6 closed — service now runs unified Program Files build, single instance, canonical ports 5005/8338). Interactive command bridge done (RemEx-8bn closed) + LaunchApp fixed (RemEx-awu closed), both via one CharSet.Unicode CreateProcessAsUser marshaling fix in WindowsActiveSession. Verified live: MONITOROFF from the Session-0 service physically turned off the monitor; LaunchApp surfaces apps in the user session. REMAINING: RemEx-fux (login GUI host still auto-launches a 2nd full host via HKCU Run; with the bridge the agent now handles power+lock+monitoroff+signout+launchapp, so the GUI host is only needed for remote-DESKTOP streaming — takeover reliability is the open piece). Recommend re-scoping fux to 'GUI host takeover reliability for remote desktop' and verifying a real cold boot.
close_reason: completed/superseded per user review

title: Agent fails to reliably reclaim the canonical port after the GUI host exits
description: Discovered verifying RemEx-fux. The single-port handoff: GUI host takes over 5005 (agent yields its web host via HostControlServer onYield), and when the GUI host disconnects the agent should reclaim (onReclaim -> AgentCoordinator.StartWebHostAsync -> HostBootstrapper.CreateApplication). Observed FLAKY: in one trial the agent reclaimed 5005 within ~6s; in another the agent process stayed alive but never resumed serving 5005 (still down after ~22s; had to restart the service to recover). Likely cause: CreateApplication's port logic falls back to 5006/5007 when 5005 is briefly busy (GUI socket still in cleanup/TIME_WAIT at the instant reclaim fires), so the agent silently rebinds a NON-canonical port -> Android client can no longer reach the host. (Alternatively onReclaim/StartWebHostAsync intermittently fails.) IMPACT: after logout or a GUI-host crash the PC becomes unreachable from the phone until the service restarts. FIX DIRECTION: in CommandAgent reclaim, bind ONLY the canonical port — wait/retry until it is free, never drift to a fallback (the StalePortReclaimer comment already warns fallback desyncs clients); ensure onReclaim always runs and logs the bound port; add a takeover->kill->reclaim integration test. Part of the epic's 'GUI-host port-takeover reliability'.
close_reason: Implemented wait loop in AgentCoordinator.StartWebHostAsync that polls IsPortFree (extracted from HostBootstrapper) up to 30s before calling CreateApplication, preventing TIME_WAIT drift to fallback ports. Fixed exception cleanup path so _app is nulled on StartAsync failure. Added 3 tests covering wait behavior, full takeover->reclaim cycle, and idempotency guard.

title: LaunchApp from Session 0 silently no-ops (cmd /c start wrapper doesn't surface cross-session)
description: Discovered while verifying RemEx-8bn. AppLauncherService.LaunchInInteractiveSession launches 'cmd.exe /c start "" /D <dir> <target>' via CreateProcessAsUser into the active console session. CreateProcessAsUser returns success and the service logs 'Launched process in interactive session 1', and the IPC/command response is success=true — but NO target process actually surfaces (verified live: triggered LaunchApp for notepad.exe and winver.exe from the Session-0 service; only cmd.exe was created and exited, the target never launched). The cmd/start (ShellExecute) indirection does not work from the Session-0 service context. This is PRE-EXISTING (the startup warning already says 'app launching will NOT work in this session') and is independent of the 8bn lock/monitor-off bridge, which launches our own exe directly (no cmd wrapper) and DOES work. Fix: in Session 0, launch the target exe directly via CreateProcessAsUser (WindowsActiveSession.TryLaunch with applicationName=target) instead of through cmd/start; for non-exe targets/shortcuts, resolve the association first or run a small in-session launcher. Note: command response should also reflect real success rather than returning success when only cmd was created.
close_reason: Resolved by the same CharSet.Unicode marshaling fix in WindowsActiveSession.TryLaunch (shared by AppLauncherService). Verified: LaunchApp of winver.exe from the Session-0 service now surfaces the app in session 1.

title: Interactive commands (Lock/MonitorOff/SignOut/desktop) need Session-1 host; Session-0 agent cannot perform them
description: WindowsSystemCommandService.Lock (LockWorkStation), MonitorOff (SendMessage broadcast), SignOut act only in the caller session; from the Session-0 LocalSystem agent they fail/no-op. They work only when the GUI host has taken over in the user session. Options (service+session-helper chosen): (a) ensure GUI-host takeover reliably completes at login; (b) route interactive commands from the agent to an in-session helper via CreateProcessAsUser/WTS — the AppLauncherService WTS pattern already exists and can be extracted into a shared IInteractiveSessionLauncher; SignOut can use WTSLogoffSession(activeSessionId) directly. At the login screen (no user) interactive commands are inherently unavailable; power commands still work.
notes: VERIFIED LIVE (2026-06-16): after the unify-build+reinstall, the RemexHost service runs the new build from C:\Program Files\RemEx as LocalSystem (Session 0). Triggered MONITOROFF over the RemExLocalIPC pipe; service logged 'SessionBridgingCommandService: Launched process in interactive session 1' — the --session-task monitoroff helper ran in the user session and executed the monitor-off broadcast. This confirms the direct CreateProcessAsUser session-task path works (lock uses the identical path; signout uses WTSLogoffSession directly). LaunchApp's separate cmd/start wrapper does NOT surface cross-session — filed as a separate pre-existing bug.
close_reason: Session-0 interactive-command bridge implemented + verified live (monitor-off turned the physical screen off via the Session-0 service).

title: Login launcher auto-starts a second full RemEx.Host (dual-host) via HKCU Run
description: HKCU Run value 'RemEx'='"C:\Program Files\RemEx\RemEx.Host.exe" --minimized' spawns a full GUI host every login while the LocalSystem service already runs the agent (was PID 6024). The single-port handoff (HostControlServer, maxNumberOfServerInstances=1) coordinates exactly one GUI host vs one agent; a stale/extra GUI host breaks it -> port fallback + pipe access-denied spam. StartupRegistrationService (in decoupled Remex.Client.Desktop) writes the entry. Make takeover robust to / guard against multiple GUI hosts.
notes: Done: added a per-session single-instance guard for the interactive GUI host (Program.cs, Local\RemExGuiHost mutex acquired before takeover; a duplicate launch exits 0 immediately). Verified live: with one agent + GUI #1 holding 5005, launching GUI #2 exits in <1s with no port collision, no 5007 fallback, agent untouched. Also verified the normal takeover/reclaim cycle works (GUI takes over 5005, exits, agent reclaims). NOTE: discovered a separate flaky-reclaim bug (filed RemEx-zq9) where the agent sometimes fails to rebind the canonical port after the GUI host dies — that is takeover-reliability (epic), not the dual-launch guard. The root dual-launch collision was already removed by the unify-build (RemEx-nx6).

title: Android RD: streaming performance (~35fps cap) — H.264 default, fps, pipeline profiling
description: Effective fps caps ~35 because default codec is MJPEG (full-frame CPU JPEG every frame). Confirm/default H.264 (FFmpeg) negotiation end-to-end on Android, raise default targetFps, and profile capture->encode->send using existing handler metrics (avgCaptureMs/avgSendMs/captured-vs-sent). Goal: materially higher fps on capable PC+phone.
notes: Performance improvements applied: (1) H264StreamDecoder: added KEY_PRIORITY=0 (real-time) and KEY_OPERATING_RATE=60f to MediaCodec hints so hardware decoder pre-allocates resources for 60fps. (2) RemoteDesktopHandler.cs: replaced per-frame elapsed-based sleep with absolute loopTimer+nextFrameTargetMs so per-frame overruns shorten the next sleep instead of accumulating as drift. Baseline: 46-50fps. These are hints/fixes not a pipeline rewrite — may need NVENC verification or further profiling if still below 60fps.

title: Android RD: dual cursor in combined virtual-desktop view (baked real cursor + Android overlay)
description: In VirtualDesktop capture the host bakes the real Windows cursor (DxgiDesktopCapture.DrawCursorOnBitmap, virtual-desktop origin) AND streams DesktopCursorState for the Android overlay, so one monitor shows the real cursor and the other the Android-drawn one. Coordinate-origin mismatch. Fix: when client SupportsCursorState, suppress host baking and draw a single Android overlay cursor using virtual-desktop coordinates.
notes: EDGE-CASE FIX IMPLEMENTED (compiles: Host build OK, compileDebugKotlin OK, host tests 207/207). Added DesktopMeta.CursorVisible (bool, default true for legacy compat). Host RemoteDesktopHandler: new IsCursorInRegion() helper; set CursorVisible on both the per-update meta (SendCursorUpdateAsync) and bootstrap meta (SendCurrentStreamBootstrapAsync) = cursor within [desktopLeft,desktopLeft+screenWidth) x [desktopTop,...). Android VM meta parser: when cursorVisible==false, set _hostCursorX/Y=-1f (hide); screen mapHostToLocal already returns null for <0 coords (also fixes pre-first-report corner-cursor glitch). Net: in single-Monitor capture the overlay hides when the pointer is on another display instead of clamping to the edge; VirtualDesktop = always in-region = always shown. Primary dual-cursor cause (host baking) already handled by drawCursor=false. Needs native rebuild (DesktopMeta is in Remex.Core->libRemexCore.so). Pending user verification of Both-screens single-cursor + off-region hide.
close_reason: Fixed dual-cursor: CursorVisible = !_drawCursor && IsCursorInRegion(...) in RemoteDesktopHandler.cs (both SendCursorUpdateAsync and SendCurrentStreamBootstrapAsync paths). Fixed left-side blank in VirtualDesktop mode: wrapped AndroidView in key(streamPixelWidth, streamPixelHeight) so the H264StreamDecoder reinitializes when switching to a wider stream; added localDecoder?.release() in onSurfaceTextureDestroyed for proper cleanup.
